corrections.was: milestone 2p, section 4 and its host row `the navigation arm tail - record`: "With no planner there is no point (node_18 == 0), so 009EE5F9 takes the skip and neither the block nor the bearing runs".
corrections.is: 009EE609 is read backwards there. The instruction is `JZ 009EE671`, and 009EE671 is the FIRST instruction of the output block: a record with no node jumps INTO the block, not past it. What +18h gates is only the lateral publish 009EE66C / 00815F30 and the two band computations above it. The block therefore runs on every pass the 009EE59B / 009EE59F gate lets through, 3426 times in the 490-step run, and it ran on all of milestone 2p's runs too - the executable was the thing skipping it.

corrections.was: docs/CRUISE_SPEED_SETTING.md and its correction in this document: "every `Cruise` unit of usn_2_java.scn authors `StartSpeed = F 12.0000`" and "the shipped mission has fourteen `Cruise` units".
corrections.is: The file has fourteen `Command = E CommandType : Cruise` lines and fourteen `StartSpeed = F 12.0000` lines, but only THIRTEEN of the Cruise lines are inside a `"Command"` sub-block. Kortenaer's sits inside its `"CamoColorGun"` sub-block and its own `"Command"` block is empty, so 004E6B30 queues nothing for it. The count of units that receive a queued `Cruise` is thirteen, which is what milestone 2n reported; the count of units that receive a `StartSpeed` seed is fourteen. Both documents are right about their own key and wrong about the other.
corrections.evidence: usn_2_java.scn lines 1098..1120; a block-aware count over the file gives Command 13, CamoColorGun 1; the run reports resolved=14 seeds but latched=13 cruise commands, and Kortenaer with no --order is in state `stop`.

corrections.was: milestone 2p, section 7: `cruise | 13 | yes, and it is 0 for every ship: nothing ordered them to move`.
corrections.is: Something did order them to move and the executable was not reading it. With 00822C20's arm run at creation the thirteen cruise ships latch a throttle of 0.657..0.741, hold 12.0 m/s and sail 294.05 m in 24.5 s and 714.12 m in 59.5 s. The `cruise` row of that table is now `yes, and it is the authored StartSpeed`.

corrections.was: milestone 2p's validation: the acceptance form `--order-frame 1 --order throttle=1,rudder=1` reproduces milestone 2j's `heading -41.252617, fwd 16.429752, yaw -0.061087` at t = 14 s.
corrections.is: It no longer does, and the reason is the seed rather than a regression. The controlled DeRuyter now starts at 12.0 m/s instead of at rest, so it reaches the saturated yaw rate sooner and has turned further by t = 14 s: heading -45.318523, fwd 16.422674, yaw -0.061087. The yaw rate is unchanged. bsp_ship_motion_probe.exe --class 20 --throttle 1 --rudder 1 from rest prints -41.253 / 16.4298 / -0.06109 at t = 14.00, which is milestone 2j's number to every printed digit, so the old figure was the from-rest answer of the same motion model.

corrections.was: include/bsp/ship_ai_goal_vector.hpp names the path record's +20h byte `more_path_20` and include/bsp/ship_ai_navigation.hpp derives `last_leg_338 = !more_path`.
corrections.is: The producer says the polarity of the NAME is inverted, though the bit itself is carried correctly. 009E3D65 and 009E419B set the byte to 1 exactly when there is no node after the successor or the outgoing leg is under one unit - that is, on the final leg - and 009E3D88 and 009E3F88 clear it when a corner is being rounded. 009EE776 SETZ then makes blk+338h true when the byte is CLEAR. So `more_path == true` marks the last leg and `last_leg_338` is set when the path continues. Nothing is mis-wired: this milestone passes the bit through unchanged. The two headers belong to other packets and are not edited here.

corrections.is: It latches blk+35Ch and writes the throttle CEILING blk+344h; it never writes blk+1D0h or blk+1D4h. 009F3F80 forms the ring command from the latch, the ceiling and the heading target.

corrections.was: not previously recorded: what a ship of this executable does when it turns.
corrections.is: It accelerates sideways. Over a 3000-step run the trajectory speed grows from 10.84 to 57.71 m/s while the forward-axis speed holds near 9 and the drift angle settles at 80 degrees. The rigid body's linear damping is zero because 00C37E00 is never called, so nothing resists the velocity the hull had before it yawed. This is a hull result, not an AI one: the twelve cruise ships hold rudder 0 and cover exactly 12.0 m/s worth of ground.
